stances.claim: Determination of probable cause during preliminary investigation is executive in nature and belongs to public prosecutors; judicial intrusion is justified only when tainted with grave abuse of discretion amounting to lack or excess of jurisdiction.
stances.rhetorical_move: Restates the operative doctrine before applying it against the CA's overreach.

stances.claim: A preliminary investigation is a 'crucial sieve in the criminal justice system' that determines 'the difference between months if not years of agonizing trial and possibly jail term, on the one hand, and peace of mind and liberty, on the other' -- necessitating careful and deliberate prosecutorial evaluation.
stances.rhetorical_move: Civil-libertarian framing of PI as the gateway protecting against pre-trial deprivation of liberty.
stances.confidence: very high -- quotes the ponencia directly

stances.claim: The powerful, the rich, and the rogue should never weaponize the law to terrorize the innocent -- the long arm of the law eventually circles back; Cornejo, Lee, and associates filed multiple capital offenses to extort millions from Navarro, and the MeTC/RTC have already convicted them of grave coercion.
stances.rhetorical_move: Moral-judicial parable framing: weaponization is recursively self-defeating.

stances.claim: The CA committed egregious overreach by reversing the DOJ (1) without Cornejo's exhaustion of administrative remedies (appeal to the Office of the President) and (2) without proper grave-abuse grounds, causing 'unwarranted arrest and detention' of Navarro -- properly corrected by the SC.
stances.rhetorical_move: Procedural-and-substantive double critique of the appellate intermediate court.

stances.claim: The Gesmundo Court's activist-libertarian streak is observable across multiple decisions (Navarro, Ditiangkin, Reyes, PCGG) and through the SPJI 2022-2027 reform program 'pursued with unprecedented passion.'
stances.rhetorical_move: Pattern-claim across multiple cases plus institutional reform; supplies the column's series-framing.

notable_anecdotes.description: Cornejo's three escalating complaints against Navarro: (1) Jan. 29, 2014 for rape allegedly on Jan. 22, 2014; (2) Feb. 27, 2014 for rape allegedly on Jan. 17, 2014, 'notably silent about the Jan. 22, 2014 incident'; (3) Oct. 16, 2015 (over a year later) for rape AND attempted rape on both Jan. 17 and Jan. 22, 2014 -- the same dates as the first and second complaints.
notable_anecdotes.purpose: Documentary inconsistency pattern that the SC used to flag the affidavits as 'strangulating.'

notable_anecdotes.description: Navarro's countercomplaints: serious illegal detention, serious physical injuries, grave threats, grave coercion, illegal arrest, blackmail-extortion (threatening to publish without payment) against Cornejo, Cedric Lee, Bernice Cua Lee, Ferdinand Guerrero, Simeon 'Zimmer' Raz Jr., Jose Paolo Gregorio Calma, Sajed Fernandez Abuhijleh, and other John Does; plus perjury complaints against Cornejo and against Cedric Lee and Raz.
notable_anecdotes.purpose: Preserves the named roll of co-conspirators and the catalog of countercharges.

notable_anecdotes.description: Recursive judicial outcome: the OCP dismissed Cornejo's three complaints for lack of probable cause; the DOJ upheld the OCP; the MeTC of Taguig convicted Cornejo, Cedric Lee, and Sajed Fernandez of grave coercion on July 27, 2018; the RTC denied their appeal on July 31, 2019 (acquitting Fernandez); the CA detoured by reversing the DOJ and ordering Navarro's arrest; the SC reversed the CA and acquitted Navarro.
notable_anecdotes.purpose: Detailed chronology demonstrating CJ's thesis that 'the long arm of the law will eventually circle back.'

notable_anecdotes.description: The 'Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovation 2022-2027' (SPJI) under the Gesmundo Court is being pursued 'with unprecedented passion' -- institutional-reform pillar alongside the named decisional pillar.
notable_anecdotes.purpose: Names the formal reform program that anchors CJ's broader activist-libertarian assessment.

one_paragraph_summary: Opening with the observation that the Gesmundo Court is 'continuing the activist and libertarian streaks of its predecessors,' CJ Panganiban catalogs four signature decisions -- Vhong Navarro v. Deniece Cornejo (Feb. 8, 2023) striking down PI weaponization, Ditiangkin v. Lazada (Sept. 21, 2022) on gig-economy classification, Reyes v. Director (Jan. 17, 2023) freeing Gigi Reyes for constitutional-rights violations, and PCGG v. Ombudsman (Jan. 17, 2023) acquitting the late Roberto Ongpin -- alongside the 'historic Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovation 2022-2027' (SPJI) being pursued 'with unprecedented passion.' The column then drills into Navarro v. Cornejo (Third Division, ponente J Henri Jean Paul B. Inting, with J Caguioa as chairperson and JJ Gaerlan, Dimaampao, and Singh concurring), reconstructing the escalating chronology: Deniece Cornejo filed three increasingly inconsistent complaints against Navarro (Jan. 29, 2014; Feb. 27, 2014; Oct. 16, 2015) covering the same Jan. 17 and Jan. 22, 2014 incidents; Navarro countersued multiple coconspirators (Cedric Lee, Bernice Cua Lee, Ferdinand Guerrero, Raz, Calma, Fernandez) for serious illegal detention, grave coercion, perjury, and extortion; the OCP and DOJ dismissed Cornejo's complaints; the MeTC and RTC of Taguig convicted Cornejo, Cedric Lee, and Fernandez of grave coercion (with Fernandez later acquitted on appeal); but the CA detoured by reversing the DOJ -- without Cornejo's required appeal to the Office of the President -- and ordering Navarro's arrest for rape. The SC's three teachings: (1) PI is executive in nature, judicial intrusion justified only on grave abuse of discretion; (2) PI is a 'crucial sieve' that 'spells the difference between months if not years of agonizing trial... and peace of mind and liberty'; (3) most important, 'the powerful, the rich, and the rogue should never weaponize the law to terrorize the innocent because the long arm of the law will eventually circle back and catch them' -- a thesis CJ shows is already vindicated by the Taguig grave-coercion convictions of Cornejo and Lee.
